confirmed.statement: S1 is explicitly called a randomized controlled experiment in both the abstract and the methods.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract ("We conducted a randomized controlled experiment (N=96) with four conditions,"); p. 4, Study design ("we carried out a randomized controlled experiment").

confirmed.statement: S1 assigns self-organized student groups to one of four conditions, supporting team assignment and a between-group design; self-organization concerns group membership.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Participants, final sentence; p. 5, Workshop Session, first paragraph and numbered condition list.

confirmed.statement: The four arms match the form: Live and Rounds without an AI peer, and Live AI and Rounds AI with an AI peer.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Workshop Session, conditions 1-4; each condition occupies a separate classroom in the following paragraph.

confirmed.statement: The assigned assistance supplies AI-generated ideas during students' own prototype brainstorming, rather than assigning participants only to evaluate outputs.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Intervention Design, paragraphs 1-3; p. 5, Workshop Session and Data collection; p. 8, Ideas' Originality, comparison of human-generated ideas between conditions.

confirmed.statement: The AI peer uses OpenAI GPT-4o to generate new ideas from the group's problem statement and participants' ideas, supporting generative_ai and ideas_supplied.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Intervention Design, first paragraph; p. 1, Abstract, identifies the peer as using a Generative Language Model.

confirmed.statement: AI throughput matches the form: two ideas per round in Rounds AI and one AI idea per three user submissions in Live AI; the peer generates initial ideas only.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Intervention Design, third paragraph.

confirmed.statement: Live sharing is immediate; round-based sharing exposes earlier rounds' ideas, with no pre-existing ideas in the first round. AI contributions are identified as AI-generated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Intervention Design, third paragraph; p. 12, AI Peers May Disrupt the Divergent Thinking Process, paragraphs on live and round-based sharing.

confirmed.statement: Condition-order randomization is inapplicable: groups receive one experimental condition, and rounds are repeated idea-sharing intervals within that condition.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Workshop Session, assignment to one of four conditions; p. 4, Intervention Design, description of rounds.

confirmed.statement: The form correctly leaves allocation counts null and qualifies the randomization claim: no sequence-generation procedure, per-arm allocation counts, or preregistration is reported.
confirmed.locator: Complete document, PDF pp. 1-17, especially pp. 4-5, Study design, Participants, and Workshop Session; references end on p. 17, with no appendix.

confirmed.statement: S1-O4 compares AI-authored and human-authored ideas from the same study; the form correctly distinguishes it from the effect of assigned AI assistance.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Ideas' Originality, paragraph preceding equation (4) and Figure 4; the paragraph separately introduces the between-condition comparison of human-generated ideas.

summary: The paper explicitly reports a randomized experiment assigning student groups to four conditions that vary collaboration format and GPT-4o assistance during their own brainstorming. The assignment, arms, and AI-tool coding are supported and criterion 1 holds, although the randomization procedure and per-arm allocation counts are unreported.
